questions.question_text: Which one of these fractions is already in simplest form?

options.why: This does simplify: $2x+10=2(x+5)$, so the $2$ cancels to leave $x+5$.
This does simplify: $3x+9=3(x+3)$, so $(x+3)$ cancels to leave $3$.
This does simplify: $x^2-25=(x-5)(x+5)$, so $(x+5)$ cancels to leave $x-5$.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{x+5}{x+10}$
Neither part factorises to give a shared factor; $x$, $5$ and $10$ are terms, not factors of the whole.
The other three each contain a common factor that cancels, so $\frac{x+5}{x+10}$ is the one in simplest form.
